items.note: The plan follows the proof at 741-765: rows 0-1 cancel the old scratch, the net target change is (JV+RG)x independent of a,c, the bit and complex coefficient checks by |S cap T|, and the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) with every scratch wire restored. The statement leaves out h=100, the indexing of X_a,Y_a by triples with stage j acting on coordinate j through v^2 separate invocations (I=3v^2), and the wire counts W_b, W_c (767-782).

It states the frames D_v, the edge operator D_v D_u^{-1}, the implemented operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}. It derives them by the paper's invariant: logical input g=D_in^{-1}f, and a common frame commutes with a pointwise R-linear gate.

Every element of the lemma's content is stated: triple-indicator lines that are nondegenerate and orthogonal for neighbours, comparable labels, the central 3->4 edges as the only decrease (loss h), L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L, orthonormal residual bases over F_2, and L/N=100/539 and 101/539. The derivation never gives the labels: the stage transitions (911-937), the gate-label table eq:motif-labels (975-988) and the residual table (1022-1043) are missing. So the nesting and the location of the only decrease are quoted rather than shown. The ambient space F^{(x)3} is also never named.

The statement covers the frames Phi_M, the permutation rho, endpoint difference I_m on every role, the shear H<-H+D, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m. The derivation is the paper's: P_V-P_U has rank dim V-dim U; the N source edges 2P_{U_a} each add rank one; the sum comes out; and P_{U_a^perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m.

The plan states that each edge's phase-frame change is a product of kernels (aI+bX_v)^{+-1}, one per orthonormal residual vector, that the residuals total s_c child calls, and (in S2.2's method) that s_c<W_c m. Missing: the frames C_U = H^{(x)m} diag(i^{q_U}) H^{(x)m}, the formula s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c, the endpoint result C^{(x)m} on every role after diagonal corrections, and the weight-additivity-mod-4 proof (1231-1315).

The plan follows the paper's route: L/N<1/2 gives deficit N-2L_b>0; both eta exceed 20*2^-50; log m<20 gives m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20*2^-50)>m(1-eta); hence s_b/W_b<m^tau. The exact eta_b=339/22587335000000 and eta_c=73/19906842167500 are not given. The complex inequality s_c/W_c<m^sigma is never stated as a claim, only implied by eta_c and tau=sigma in S5.1.1.1.

It states the four elementary operations and the controlled shifts and unit scalings at O(V), with no derivation of the proofs (513-550, 574-621). S2.1.2's claim leaves out the hypotheses: q prime, coefficient denominators prime to q, and offsets prepared in b^{O(1)} time. The last appears only in its quote.

The statement has A=E_1 Pi E_2, with E_1, E_2 invertible lower triangular and Pi a partial permutation with a ones, and the shear done with exactly a interchanges plus O(V). The derivation follows both proofs step by step: pivot at the topmost row's rightmost entry, an odd prime q avoiding the table's denominators and diagonal numerators, triangular updates in descending order, and the three-update interchange trick.

Every step of the proof of prop:power-interchange is here: k=0 by a digit operation, m fields of b=e/m digits, a cyclic row split into W role streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} on each edge by recursive interchanges, H<-H+D on every row, then D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D. It continues with s calls on volume V/W, O(V) overhead, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the two-case geometric sum, and the fixed-tape parking schedule.

It follows the paper's route: rho=O(log e) high digits exchanged and joined into a row field R=q^{2rho}>=W^k, padding to a multiple of W^k, base-m pieces handled by the power-width procedure at total O(Ve^tau), then binary ranges padded to [q^e]. Separating the high parts at the end is not spelled out. The unequal-width remark (1740-1762) is used only later (S4.2.5).

Present: C=HSH=aI+bX and its identities, P_M X_v P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv}, inverse children via (C^{-1})^{(x)f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, exactly s_c child calls, and H_0^{(x)D}=b^D S_D C^{(x)D} S_D. Missing is the exact recursive contract (1903-1916): the network with column frames, the Z_{a,f} and i^{27f} endpoint corrections and the undone bank exchange give C^{(x)e} on every role. Without it the plan never says what the s_c calls compute.

The proof is followed closely: eight conditional additions giving (u+c(1-2(u mod 2)), w), one cyclic shift per line, the guard interval, the union bound for delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^-K}, repair of T_0 S_0^{-1} on B by radix sort, and the top position by a two-bit XOR. The headline claims O(V(L^tau+1)) outright, without the family hypotheses (A=O(p), R superpolynomial, K/log p->infinity) under which the paper reduces eq:packed-rectangle-time to that bound.

It covers s calls per node, the O(V((eK)^tau+1)) overhead from packed additions, rows from the first q_0 chunks with range >=W^{k_0}, the row split u=Wg+w with child volume V/W, and F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with F(e)=O(e) at the leaves. It then bounds internal costs by O(e^lambda) and leaves by O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), and sums the base-m pieces to O(d^{lambda'}). This is the paper's route.

The proof then adds the total time, the conversion through S_D and the disk-preserving truncation. It covers V=Tp, the margins g_1..g_7, min g_i=g_2=2^-181=2kappa, row-by-row justification, setup and exceptional sorting as o(V), the 2kappa slack absorbing powers of log p, O(n(log n)^{1-kappa}) and the schoolbook cutoff, as in the paper. No step mentions the Schonhage-Strassen conjecture, an eventual lower bound, or the liminf condition. The plan stops at the time bound (S0, S6.12).

errors.says: Three invocations of a fixed schedule of linear gates exchange the two banks X,Y up to sign and restore every scratch wire.
errors.paper: There are three stages. Stage j fixes the other two coordinates and acts on coordinate j through v^2 separate invocations, each with its own auxiliary wires, so I=3v^2 invocations in all. This count enters W and L=Ich.

errors.says: Adding the selected bits of one chunk into another costs O(V(L^tau+1)) with a constant number of cyclic shifts plus a deterministic repair.
errors.paper: The lemma's bound is O(V(L^tau+1)+M A_rect^3+delta_bad M A_rect(R+A_rect)). It reduces to O(V(L^tau+1)) only when A_rect=O(p), R exceeds every fixed polynomial in p, f<=d<=p and K/log p->infinity.

chain: The tree reaches O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) by the paper's route. S2.1 builds the interchange from the bit network: labels, rank budget, shear interface, matrix shear, then the recurrence with tau=1-2^-50. S2.2 builds the simultaneous layer from the complex network, S3 the synthetic convolution, and S4 the resampling with chirp and permutation cancellation. S5 assembles the algorithm and proves exact recovery, and S6 gives the cost table with min margin 2^-181=2kappa. The plan thins out at three points: the label construction (gate-label and residual tables only quoted), the complex phase interface (C_U, the weight-additivity proof, s_c's formula and the endpoint C^{(x)m} missing), and the recursive contract that the complex network returns C^{(x)e}. The conjecture-negation remark is absent.

steps.note: The fixed linear network is fully there: gate schedule, coefficient check by triple intersection, (x,y)->(-y,x), and every scratch wire restored whatever its initial value. It is short on parameters: h=100, the triple indexing of X_a,Y_a, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are never stated. N appears only as the number of data wires per bank and m only as the label dimension with m<2^20. That is a borderline call: the mechanism and its role are present, the sizes are not.

It says that a common frame per gate commutes with the pointwise gate, that the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and that each edge costs only a change of frame. S2.1.5.8 applies this with Phi_M frames on the role streams.

Present: nondegenerate labels built from triple-indicator vectors in a space of dimension m, comparable labels on every edge, and the central 3->4 edges as the only decrease, each removing P(x)F(x)Q of dimension h. The ambient F^{(x)3} and the label table are cited rather than given.
It states that P_V-P_U has rank dim V-dim U for nested U in V, so an edge costs its label's dimension change. The N source edges with matrix 2P_{U_a} are the rank-one exceptions.
The signed changes telescope to Wm-2N; with L=Ich, the absolute changes sum to Wm-2N+2L; adding the N source ranks gives s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
It gives L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2, so the deficit N-2L_b>0 and s_b<W_b m.

It gives the endpoint difference P_{U_a^perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m for X_a, and zero source with identity sink for the other roles. With rho, the bit network therefore applies H<-H+D on every role, scratch rows included.
A shear by a rank-a matrix factors as E_1 Pi E_2 and costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V). Each node therefore makes exactly s recursive calls, the sum of the edge ranks.
Children have volume V/W, so F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1). The paper's comparison then gives s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^-50, from eta>20*2^-50 and log m<20, and hence F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan reconstructs all nine steps of the central saving in the paper's order and roles: network (S2.1.3), frames (S2.1.4), labels and budget (S2.1.5.1), rank equals dimension change plus the N source ranks (S2.1.5.2), strict saving from L/N<1/2, endpoint identity giving H<-H+D, the E_1 Pi E_2 shear costing exactly rank-many calls, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^-50. The only thinning is in C1, where h=100, N and m=h^3 are not stated explicitly, and in C3, where the label table is cited rather than given.
